title: Local fibre dimension inequality for a composite
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ and $g:Y\to T$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme], both locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. For $x\in X$, put $y=f(x)$ and $t=g(y)$. Write $X_t$, $X_y$ and $Y_t$ for the scheme-theoretic fibres of $g\circ f$, $f$ and $g$, respectively [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. For the topological dimensions at the indicated points [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point], one has $\dim_x(X_t)\leq\dim_x(X_y)+\dim_y(Y_t)$. No flatness hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Set $s=t$ in the notation of the source and restrict to affine neighbourhoods of $x$, $y$ and $t$. Because $f$ and $g$ are locally of finite type, the three fibre schemes $X_t$, $X_y$ and $Y_t$ are locally of finite type over the residue fields $\kappa(t)$ and $\kappa(y)$; their affine neighbourhoods have finite-type coordinate algebras. The fibre-product affine-spectrum identification [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] identifies these coordinate rings with the corresponding tensor products and identifies the residue-field maps. The local rings occurring below are Noetherian by [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft], applied to the finite-type morphisms to the spectra of fields.

source.place: Tag 02JS, proof: reduction to affine neighbourhoods and the three fibre schemes

proof.text: For a point in a finite-type affine neighbourhood of a fibre, apply the finite-type dimension formula [lem-kun-dimension-formula]: the topological local dimension is the Krull dimension of the corresponding local ring plus the transcendence degree of its residue field over the base residue field. Apply this to $X_t$ at $x$, $X_y$ at $x$, and $Y_t$ at $y$. The open-subspace invariance [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-at-point-open-subspace] lets us replace each whole fibre by the chosen affine neighbourhood without changing the indicated local dimension.

source.place: Tag 02JS proof, using Tag 02FX (lemma-dimension-fibre-at-a-point) on the three fibres

proof.text: Choose affine neighbourhoods of the three points in the fibre schemes, and write $A=\mathcal O_{Y_t,y}$ and $B=\mathcal O_{X_t,x}$. The composite-fibre-local-model statement [lem-sbc-composite-fibre-local-models] verifies that these are Noetherian local rings, that the induced map $A\to B$ is local, and that its closed fibre is canonically $B/\mathfrak m_A B\cong\mathcal O_{X_y,x}$. Applying [lem-trf-local-fibre-ring-dimension-inequality] to the corresponding primes gives $\dim B\leq\dim A+\dim(B/\mathfrak m_A B)$, exactly the local-ring inequality required in the 02JS proof.

source.place: Tag 02JS proof, reduced to Algebra Tag 00OM (lemma-dimension-base-fibre-total)

proof.text: The residue fields form the tower $\kappa(t)\subseteq\kappa(y)\subseteq\kappa(x)$. Hence [lem-sbc-transcendence-degree-tower] gives $\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(t)}\kappa(x)=\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(y)}\kappa(x)+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(t)}\kappa(y)$ (ordinary addition here, since the finite-type fibre dimensions are finite). Substitute this identity into the local-ring inequality from Step 3 and use the three equalities from Step 2; the intermediate terms regroup as $\dim_x(X_y)+\dim_y(Y_t)$, yielding $\dim_x(X_t)\leq\dim_x(X_y)+\dim_y(Y_t)$. Empty fibres cause no issue, and no flatness was used.

source.place: Tag 02JS proof, transcendence-degree tower and final substitution

proof_origin.place: Tag 02JS, lemma-dimension-fibre-at-a-point-additive, proof via Tag 02FX and Algebra Tag 02IJ
